Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

terrible adjective

causing fear, dreadful

also dreadful, frightening, fearsome, horrifying

classical

Cic. Sest. 19 (Lewis & Short): quam terribilis aspectū!
Traupman 392: terribilis, terrible

terribilis, terribile

adjective, third declension

terrible, frightening

From terreō: what strikes terror, in looks, sound or power.

Other words

  • horribilis, horribile — horrible, dreadful

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.4.1: horribile est quae loquantur, quae minitentur; Traupman 154

    What makes one shudder (horrēre); in Cicero’s letters and Catullus also simply “awful, very bad” (see terrible, very bad).

  • dīrus, dīra, dīrum — dreadful, dire, ill-omened

    adjective · also used · classical · Traupman 149, 151: dīrus, awful, dreadful

    Properly of evil omen; so fearful, awful, and of people cruel (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • horribile est quae loquantur, quae minitentur.

    it is terrible what they say, what they threaten.Cic. Att. 14.4.1

  • madidīs Notus ēvolat ālīs, terribilem piceā tēctus cālīgine vultum

    the South Wind flies out on dripping wings, his terrible face veiled in pitch-black mistOv. M. 1.264–269

  • major ignōtārum rērum est terror

    things we don’t know frighten us moreLiv. 28.44.3

See also terrible, be afraid, frighten.
